title: Health Check Endpoints for Agents
summary: Separate process survival, traffic readiness, and end-to-end agent capability so health automation makes the correct recovery decision.
overview: An agent health endpoint exposes a deliberately narrow claim about its ability to operate. Liveness asks whether the process can make local progress; readiness asks whether it should receive new work; startup asks whether initialization has completed. End-to-end synthetic checks ask a different question: can a representative task succeed across its dependencies?

Combining these signals into one deep probe creates dangerous feedback. A provider outage can make every agent fail liveness, causing restarts that destroy warm state without repairing the provider. Health handlers should be cheap, bounded, and independent of the same saturated execution pool they are diagnosing.

production.poc: A prototype can expose a process heartbeat and a manual sample-task check to reveal the distinction between reachability and usefulness.
production.production: Production defines separate endpoints, startup allowances, readiness thresholds, and graceful draining for active tasks.
production.scale: At fleet scale, probe traffic itself needs budgeting, synthetic tests need safe test tenants, and alerting must distinguish local failure from shared dependency incidents.

components.name: Liveness handler
components.role: Checks local event-loop or worker progress without calling remote model providers.

components.name: Readiness evaluator
components.role: Reports configuration validity, required local resources, and admission capacity.

components.name: Startup gate
components.role: Prevents normal probes from interrupting legitimate initialization or model loading.

components.name: Synthetic task runner
components.role: Exercises an approved read-only workflow with known expected outcomes.

components.name: Traffic controller
components.role: Removes unready instances and respects draining before termination.

flow.title: Initialize under startup gate
flow.description: Load configuration, connect durable state, and complete any required model warmup.

flow.title: Publish readiness
flow.description: Allow traffic only when the instance can admit work under its documented dependency policy.

flow.title: Probe local progress
flow.description: Respond to liveness using a cheap signal that detects an unrecoverable local stall.

flow.title: Run synthetic capability checks
flow.description: Periodically execute a separate safe task and classify dependency and semantic failures.

flow.title: Drain before replacement
flow.description: Stop accepting new tasks, checkpoint active work, and honor a bounded shutdown grace period.

flow.title: Correlate fleet signals
flow.description: Compare per-instance failures with regional dependency status before triggering broad remediation.

diagrams.title: Three health decisions
diagrams.code:
flowchart TD
 K["Container supervisor"] --> S["Startup complete"]
 S --> L["Local progress probe"]
 L --> R["Restart stalled process"]
 T["Traffic controller"] --> Q["Ready to admit work"]
 Q --> D["Drain unready instance"]
 M["Synthetic task monitor"] --> A["Agent plus dependencies"]
 A --> I["Capability incident"]
diagrams.caption: Restarting a process, withholding new traffic, and declaring a service incident require different evidence.

diagrams.title: Lifecycle of serving readiness
diagrams.code:
stateDiagram-v2
 [*] --> Starting
 Starting --> Ready: Initialization and warmup pass
 Ready --> Draining: Shutdown or capacity withdrawal
 Draining --> Stopped: Active work finishes
 Ready --> Unready: Cannot admit new work
 Unready --> Ready: Admission recovers
 Ready --> Failed: Local progress stalls
 Failed --> Starting: Supervisor replaces instance
 Stopped --> [*]
diagrams.caption: Readiness withdrawal can preserve a live process while a local stall justifies replacement.

useCase.title: Customer support agent health during a billing outage
useCase.situation: A support platform runs many agent replicas that answer product questions and retrieve customer bills.
useCase.problem: A billing outage affects one capability while product information remains available.
useCase.requirement: Continue safe product assistance and clearly defer billing work without restarting every replica.
useCase.architecture: Local probes feed the container platform; a capability monitor checks a synthetic billing account and publishes degraded billing status.
runtime: A billing synthetic fails while local liveness remains healthy.
The router disables billing-dependent tasks and leaves product-question capacity available.
useCase.failure: If the event loop actually stalls, the liveness controller replaces only that instance after its failure threshold.
useCase.impact: Track capability availability, false restart rate, and task loss during drain; process uptime alone cannot represent user-visible availability.

tradeoffs.benefit: Avoids restart storms during shared outages.
tradeoffs.cost: Cannot prove that the full agent workflow succeeds.

tradeoffs.benefit: Avoids admitting work an instance cannot handle.
tradeoffs.cost: Overly strict checks can remove otherwise useful capacity.
Consume quota and require maintained safe fixtures.

failures.detection: Health latency rises with executor saturation.
failures.recovery: Isolate health handling and bound admission to the work pool.

failures.detection: Startup never reaches completion before probe thresholds expire.
failures.recovery: Measure startup distribution and configure a distinct startup budget.

mistakes.mistake: Calling the model on every liveness probe
mistakes.fix: Use local progress for liveness and a scheduled synthetic for model capability.

mistakes.mistake: Returning detailed secrets in health output
mistakes.fix: Expose minimal public status and protect diagnostic details.
Make readiness fail first, then drain active jobs before termination.

whenToUse: Use for agents managed by containers or process supervisors.
Use when one agent exposes several independently degradable capabilities.
Use before enabling automatic replacement or autoscaling.
whenNotToUse: Do not use liveness as a business-quality score.
Avoid expensive inference on high-frequency probes.
Avoid declaring unready for optional dependencies with valid fallback behavior.
checklist: Keep liveness free of remote calls.
Test graceful drain with active tool calls.
Monitor synthetic tasks separately from container status.
